### Building a New Desktop PC – A Step‑by‑Step Guide *(No special software or external APIs required)* --- #### 1️⃣ Plan & Budget | Category | What you’ll decide | |----------|--------------------| | **Purpose** | Gaming, content creation, office work, etc. | | **Budget** | Rough ranges:
• $500–$800 — entry‑level gaming
• $900–$1500 — mid‑range / high‑end gaming
• >$2000 — enthusiast/overclocking | | **Future Proofing** | Consider future upgrades (e.g., extra PCI‑E slots, more USB ports). | *Tip:* Use online “PC builder” sites (PCPartPicker, BuildMyPC) to see price comparisons and detect incompatibilities before purchasing. --- #### 2️⃣ Pick Your Components Below is an example list for a solid mid‑tier system (~$1200): | Component | Example Part | Why it’s good | |-----------|--------------|---------------| | **CPU** | AMD Ryzen 5 5600X | 6 cores, great single‑thread performance | | **Motherboard** | MSI B550-A PRO | AM4 socket, supports DDR4, decent VRM | | **RAM** | Corsair Vengeance LPX 16GB (2×8GB) DDR4‑3200 | Dual‑channel, low profile | | **GPU** | NVIDIA RTX 3060 Ti | Excellent 1080p/1440p gaming | | **Storage** | Samsung 970 EVO Plus 1TB NVMe SSD | Fast boot + game load times | | **Power Supply** | EVGA SuperNOVA 650 G5 | 80+ Gold certified, fully modular | | **Case** | NZXT H510 | Mid‑tower, cable management friendly | | **Cooling** | Stock cooler (included w/Ryzen 5) OR Cooler Master Hyper 212 RGB | Keeps temps under control | | **Operating System** | Windows 10 Home OEM key (or free Linux distro) | Most games run best on Windows | Make sure: - **Socket matches:** e.g., AM4 for Ryzen CPUs. - **Form factor fits:** ATX motherboards fit most cases; mini‑ITX needs smaller cases. - **PSU wattage ≥ total TDP + margin (usually +30%).** Use *PCPartPicker*’s “Compatibility Checker” to catch mismatches early. --- #### 3️⃣ Gather Tools & Workspace - Phillips #2 screwdriver (most screws use this head). - Anti‑static wrist strap (optional but recommended). - Small container for screws. - Clean, flat surface (desk or table). --- #### 4️⃣ Assemble the Motherboard First 1. **Install the CPU** - Lift the CPU socket lever. - Align the triangle corner of the processor with the socket marker. - Place gently → lock lever down. 2. **Apply Thermal Paste** *(if not pre‑applied)* - Tiny pea‑size dot at center of CPU. 3. **Mount the CPU Cooler** - Attach mounting brackets per manual. - Secure fan(s); connect PWM or 12V header later. 4. **Insert RAM** - Unlock DIMM slots. - Snap sticks into place until clicks sound. 5. **Place M.2 SSD** (if using) - Slide into slot, tighten screw. 6. **Attach I/O Shield** - Fit metal plate into back panel holes of your case. 7. **Prep Power Connections** - Plug 24‑pin main PSU connector onto motherboard. - Connect 8‑pin EPS (for CPU). --- #### 5️⃣ Mount the Case & Install the Motherboard 1. **Secure standoffs** inside the case matching motherboard layout. 2. **Lift motherboard** carefully over standoff grid. 3. **Align with I/O shield**, then secure with screws. --- #### 6️⃣ Add Expansion Cards & Storage - **Graphics Card** - Insert into top PCI‑E x16 slot. - Lock bracket, attach screws. - Connect one or two 8‑pin GPU power cables from PSU. - **Additional Drives** - SATA drives: mount in drive bays, connect data + power cables. --- #### 7️⃣ Cable Management - Route cables behind motherboard tray where possible. - Keep airflow unobstructed: front fans intake air, rear exhaust out. - Use zip ties or Velcro straps to bundle excess length. --- #### 8️⃣ Final Checks Before Boot | Check | How | |-------|-----| | All screws tightened | Don’t overtighten! | | Fans spin when powered | Verify orientation (intake vs exhaust). | | PSU switch off | Ensure no accidental short. | | Monitor connected via HDMI/DVI/VGA | Confirm correct port on GPU. | --- #### 9️⃣ Power On & Enter BIOS 1. Switch PSU ON. 2. Press **Del/F2** during POST to enter BIOS. 3. Verify detected hardware: CPU speed, RAM frequency, storage devices. 4. Set boot priority to your installation media (USB/DVD). 5. Save changes & exit. --- #### 🔟 Install Operating System - Create bootable USB (Rufus, BalenaEtcher). - Follow installer prompts: partition disk, format as NTFS, install drivers after first boot. After OS installs: 1. Update all drivers (chipset, graphics, audio). 2. Run benchmark tests (Cinebench R23, 3DMark) to confirm temperatures stay below ~70°C under load. 3. Adjust fan curves in BIOS or through software (MSI Afterburner, SpeedFan). --- #### 🛠️ Troubleshooting Common Issues | Symptom | Likely Cause | Fix | |---------|-------------|-----| | No display | Wrong GPU slot, missing power cable, faulty monitor connection | Recheck connections, try another slot | | Overheating immediately | Poor thermal paste application, inadequate ventilation | Reapply paste, improve airflow | | Random freezes | Insufficient PSU capacity, unstable memory | Upgrade PSU, test RAM with MemTest86 | | BIOS doesn’t recognize GPU | Incorrect BIOS settings (PCI-E mode), outdated firmware | Enable Auto or Gen3, update BIOS | --- #### 📌 Quick Checklist Summary ``` [ ] CPU installed correctly [ ] Cooling solution attached [ ] RAM seated properly [ ] M.2 SSD inserted [ ] Motherboard mounted on standoffs [ ] PSU connectors plugged in [ ] GPU secured and powered [ ] Cables routed neatly [ ] Front/back panels closed [ ] Monitor & peripherals ready [ ] BIOS set to boot from USB [ ] OS installed & updated ``` --- ### 🎉 Congratulations! Your brand‑new PC is now up and running. Enjoy customizing further—add RGB lighting, upgrade storage, tweak overclocks—but always keep temperature monitoring handy. Happy building!
